lessons.title: Multi-Agent Systems
lessons.summary: Understand multi-agent systems by comparing mechanisms and applying them to practical scenarios. Reading does not establish assessment mastery.

sections.title: Roles
paragraphs: Coordinator: Assigns and integrates work under an overall goal.
Specialist: Handles a bounded domain or subtask.
Reviewer: Checks outputs against explicit criteria.
Shared service: Provides a common capability without becoming an independent decision-maker.

sections.title: Coordination
paragraphs: Delegation: Assigns a task with scope and expected output.
Handoff: Transfers responsibility and necessary context.
Aggregation: Combines compatible outputs into a result.
Conflict resolution: Handles incompatible findings explicitly.

sections.title: Communication
paragraphs: Task contract: Defines input, scope and success criteria.
Message provenance: Records which participant produced a claim.
Shared state rule: Specifies how updates are validated and combined.
Context selection: Supplies only relevant information within budget.

sections.title: Risk controls
paragraphs: Permission isolation: Each worker receives only necessary access.
Budget allocation: Bounds total and per-worker resource use.
Loop detection: Identifies repeated delegation without progress.
Independent validation: Uses evidence beyond agents agreeing with one another.

sections.title: Design evaluation
paragraphs: Single-agent baseline: Measures whether simpler execution already meets the need.
Parallel benefit: Independent work can reduce elapsed time when coordination cost is justified.
Coordination overhead: Communication and integration add latency and cost.
End-to-end evaluation: Measures the final task outcome rather than only individual worker quality.

lessons.title: Fine-Tuning

sections.title: Adaptation choices
paragraphs: Prompting: Changes supplied instructions without updating model weights.
Retrieval: Supplies external evidence at inference time.
Fine-tuning: Updates learned parameters using a training objective.
Evaluation: Measures behavior on held-out representative cases.

sections.title: Dataset partitions
paragraphs: Training set: Provides examples used to update weights.
Validation set: Supports tuning choices without becoming the final unbiased test.
Test set: Measures final performance on held-out examples.
Leakage: Information from evaluation cases contaminates training or selection.

sections.title: Training signals
paragraphs: Loss: Quantifies error under the selected objective.
Gradient: Indicates parameter sensitivity to the objective.
Learning rate: Controls update step size.
Epoch: Represents a pass through the training dataset.

sections.title: Generalization
paragraphs: Overfitting: Training improves while unseen-case performance deteriorates.
Underfitting: The model fails to learn sufficient task structure.
Distribution shift: Deployment inputs differ materially from training data.
Catastrophic forgetting: Adaptation degrades previously useful learned behavior.

sections.title: Release checks
paragraphs: Task benchmark: Measures the intended behavior against a baseline.
Safety regression: Tests whether adaptation harms important restrictions.
Data provenance: Records sources, permissions and preparation of examples.
Model artifact record: Records base model, configuration and resulting checkpoint.

sections.title: Core mechanism
paragraphs: Frozen base: Original model weights remain unchanged during adapter training.
Low-rank update: Trainable factors represent a constrained weight update.
Adapter: Stores task-specific learned parameters separately.
Full fine-tuning: Updates the selected original model parameters directly.

sections.title: Configuration
paragraphs: Rank: Controls the dimensional capacity of each low-rank update.
Scaling: Controls the contribution of the adapter update.
Target modules: Select where adapters are inserted.
Dropout: Randomly drops activations during training under the configured rule.

sections.title: Resource use
paragraphs: Trainable parameter saving: Fewer learned parameters reduce optimizer-state needs.
Base residency: The underlying model still consumes memory.
Activation cost: Intermediate training tensors still require memory.
Inference merge: Compatible adapter weights may be combined with base weights under supported conditions.

sections.title: Compatibility
paragraphs: Base identity: Use the exact compatible underlying model.
Module compatibility: Match the targeted architecture and layer names.
Adapter version: Record the learned parameter artifact being used.
Evaluation contract: Check task behavior after loading or merging.

sections.title: Tradeoffs
paragraphs: Capacity tradeoff: Lower rank can constrain adaptation expressiveness.
Task specificity: An adapter's gains are measured for its intended distribution.
Empirical comparison: Benchmark against alternatives instead of assuming superiority.
Permission review: The base and dataset still have applicable usage conditions.

lessons.title: QLoRA
lessons.summary: Understand qlora by comparing mechanisms and applying them to practical scenarios. Reading does not establish assessment mastery.

sections.title: Components
paragraphs: Quantized base: Stores frozen base weights in a lower-bit representation.
LoRA factors: Trainable low-rank parameters adapt the model.
Quantization configuration: Specifies weight representation and associated settings.
Compute dtype: Controls arithmetic precision rather than merely stored weight width.

sections.title: Paper techniques
paragraphs: NF4: A four-bit format designed around normally distributed weights.
Double quantization: Quantizes quantization constants to reduce memory overhead.
Paged optimizer: Uses memory-management techniques to handle optimizer memory spikes.
Low-rank adaptation: Trains smaller factors rather than all original parameters.

sections.title: Memory boundaries
paragraphs: Weight storage: Memory used to hold model parameters.
Optimizer state: Memory used for training optimizer bookkeeping.
Activations: Memory used for intermediate tensors during training.
Runtime workspace: Additional memory required by kernels and execution.

sections.title: Compatibility
paragraphs: Hardware support: The runtime must support required low-bit operations.
Base match: Adapters must match the underlying model architecture and identity.
Dtype support: Chosen arithmetic precision must be supported by the environment.
Artifact metadata: Record model, adapter and quantization settings together.

sections.title: Claims and evaluation
paragraphs: Measured quality: Evaluate adapted outputs on held-out task cases.
Resource measurement: Measure actual memory and execution cost.
Scope limitation: A method's reported results do not guarantee all models and tasks.
Deployment verification: Test the intended serving configuration after training.

sections.title: Deployment choices
paragraphs: Local inference: Runs model computation on infrastructure under the operator's control.
Hosted API: Uses a remote service for model execution.
Model weights: Parameters must be obtained and loaded for local execution.
Runtime: Software executes the model on supported hardware.

sections.title: Memory planning
paragraphs: Weight memory: Stores the loaded model parameters.
KV cache: Retains attention-related state for active token sequences.
Batch memory: Concurrent sequences increase runtime state needs.
Headroom: Reserve additional capacity for execution and nonmodel processes.

sections.title: Optimization
paragraphs: Quantization: Uses lower-precision parameter representations with possible quality tradeoffs.
Batching: Groups compatible requests to improve resource utilization.
Offloading: Moves some data or computation between available devices.
Context control: Limits active input/history to manage costs and capacity.

sections.title: Trust and permissions
paragraphs: License check: Determine permitted model uses and redistribution conditions.
Artifact provenance: Verify the origin and integrity of downloaded model files.
Data handling: Control logs and storage even when inference is local.
Network boundary: Inspect telemetry, downloads and integrations rather than assume offline operation.

sections.title: Serving evaluation
paragraphs: Quality benchmark: Measures task performance with representative inputs.
Latency: Measures response time including token generation.
Throughput: Measures completed work per unit time under load.
Reliability: Measures failed requests and stable operation over time.
